Set up reproducible release builds: containerized build environments with pinned compilers for each supported Linux architecture, a CI pipeline that builds and runs the unit tests from one tagged commit, produces versioned, checksummed release artifacts (static where possible) and publishes them to the release page, plus a note on how the macOS and BSD builds are handled since containers cannot produce those natively.

generic_title: Package and distribute a C++ desktop application
generic_prompt: I have finished a C++ (CMake) desktop GUI application and it runs fine from my IDE, but I do not know how to hand it to people who do not have my development setup. Add packaging so a release produces installable artifacts for end users: bundle or declare the required shared libraries and plugins, produce a Windows installer and a Linux package or portable bundle, set version metadata, and add a CI step that builds these artifacts and verifies they launch on a clean machine.
title: Distributable packages for the status bar
prompt: In this X11 desktop status bar, users have to build from source with a long list of system libraries. Add packaging so each release produces installable artifacts: distribution packages that declare the needed runtime libraries (xcb, cairo, audio and network modules) as dependencies with optional modules split out, a portable bundle for other distributions, proper version metadata and default config installation, and a CI step that builds them and verifies the bar starts on a clean machine.

generic_title: Ship a dynamically linked Linux app across distributions
generic_prompt: My C++ (CMake) application must link its GUI framework dynamically for license compliance, so I cannot ship a single static binary. Package it so it runs across common Linux distributions: decide between native distro packages and a self-contained portable bundle format, set rpath/library lookup correctly, declare or bundle dependent shared libraries, and add a CI job that builds the packages and runs the app on several distribution images.
title: Cross-distribution Linux packages for the CLI
prompt: In this todo / task management CLI, the C++ binary links a Rust storage library and system libraries, and users on older distributions struggle to install it. Add release packaging for Linux: native distribution packages plus a self-contained portable bundle, correct rpath/library lookup for dynamically linked dependencies, shell completions and man pages installed in the right places, and a CI job that builds the packages and runs a basic add/list/done smoke test on several distribution images.

generic_title: Deploy a C++ game server to a Linux box without its libraries
generic_prompt: I wrote a small client-server game in C++ (CMake); the server works on my machine but fails on a Linux server that lacks the networking libraries, and static linking hits system C library version errors. Set up a reliable deployment: package the server with its runtime dependencies in an isolated, reproducible image or bundle built against a compatible baseline, run it as a supervised service with restart on failure, expose its port, and document a one-command deploy and rollback.
title: Deploy the search server and crawler to a Linux host
prompt: In this small-web protocol search engine, the server and crawler only run on machines where all native dependencies were installed by hand. Set up a reproducible deployment: build the server and crawler into isolated images built against a compatible baseline with their runtime libraries, run them as supervised services with restart on failure alongside the index database, expose the server port, schedule the crawler, and document a one-command deploy and rollback.

generic_title: Host a C++ web service on a managed platform
generic_prompt: I have a C++ (CMake) application that I want to run online as a web service. Get it deployed on a managed hosting platform: build it into a deployable artifact or container image, bind to the port supplied by the platform environment, read configuration from environment variables, add a health check endpoint, and set up automatic deploys from the main branch. Compare a couple of hosting options and explain the choice.
title: Host the search engine on a managed platform
prompt: In this small-web protocol search engine, the web server is run manually on a personal machine. Get it running online on a managed hosting platform: build the server into a deployable container image, bind to the platform-provided port and read database connection settings and other config from environment variables, add a health check, connect it to a managed relational database for the index, and set up automatic deploys from the main branch. Compare a couple of hosting options and explain the choice.

generic_title: Deploy a C++ service built with newer dependencies to an older server
generic_prompt: My C++ (CMake) service depends on a newer compiler, a database client driver and general-purpose libraries. I develop on a newer Linux release but must deploy on an older server where I cannot compile dependencies. Keep deployment simple and repeatable: choose between static linking, bundling shared libraries, or shipping an isolated runtime image, implement it in the build, and add a CI job that builds the release on the newer toolchain and verifies it starts on the older target.
title: Deploy the TTS server to older Linux hosts
prompt: In this streaming text-to-speech server, the build needs a modern compiler plus native libraries for the inference runtime, phonemizer and audio encoding, and the target servers run an older Linux release where these cannot be built. Keep deployment repeatable: choose between bundling shared libraries, partial static linking, or an isolated runtime image with the model files, implement it in the build, and add a CI job that builds the release and verifies the server starts and synthesizes a test sentence on the older target.

generic_title: Add a natural-language assistant that answers questions about project tasks
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot project-management API, I want a simple chat assistant endpoint. Users type questions like "give me all completed tasks so far", "show me the last completed task" or "list my pending tasks", and the assistant should figure out the intent, call our existing task service methods as tools (filtering by status, owner and date), and reply with the matching tasks plus a short summary. Right now we use a regex dictionary with a full-text fallback, which breaks on any rephrasing. Scope answers to the current user, refuse questions outside project data, and add tests for a few phrasings of each question.
title: Add a natural-language assistant that answers questions about dashboards and reports
prompt: In this BI / SQL reporting dashboards app, I want a chat assistant endpoint where a signed-in user can ask things like "which dashboards did I edit last week", "show the reports that use the sales datasource" or "list dashboards shared with my group". The assistant should interpret the question, call the existing dashboard, report and datasource lookup code as tools (respecting the user's permissions), and answer with the matching items plus a short summary. It must not run arbitrary SQL itself, should decline questions outside the app's metadata, and needs tests for several phrasings of each question.

generic_title: Build user-managed recurring schedules for reminder tasks
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service, I need an embedded scheduler at the heart of a web-based reminder system for an elderly relative who must eat and take insulin on a strict schedule. Through a REST API, a remote caregiver should be able to add, change and delete tasks that fire monthly, weekly, daily or at a specific time of day; each task shows a message and plays an audio file on the local machine. Schedules must survive restarts, misfires after downtime should be handled sensibly (fire once, not dozens of times), and changes must take effect without restarting the service.
title: Let users schedule recurring report runs for dashboards
prompt: In this BI / SQL reporting dashboards app, I want users to schedule reports to run on a recurring basis: monthly, weekly, daily, or at a specific time of day. Through the API a user should be able to create, edit, pause and delete a schedule for one of their reports; when it fires, the report's queries run in the background and the result snapshot is stored for later viewing. Schedules must be persisted and survive restarts, missed runs after downtime should fire once rather than piling up, two app instances must not run the same schedule twice, and edits take effect without a restart.

generic_title: Log every HTTP request and response as one structured entry
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot REST API, I need every request logged in a single place as one structured entry: HTTP status, path, method, query string, client IP, the controller method that handled it, its arguments, the response body, and, for failures, the exception type, message, a generated exception ID and stack trace. Success and error cases (including ones handled by exception handlers) must produce the same shape of entry. Access tokens and passwords must be redacted, large bodies truncated, and the entries should be shippable to a central log aggregation backend.
title: Log every shortener API request and response as one structured entry
prompt: In this URL shortener app, I need every request to the shorten and redirect endpoints logged in one place as a single structured entry: HTTP status, path, method, client IP, the handler method, its arguments (e.g. the original URL), the response (the short code or redirect target) and, on errors such as an unknown code, the exception type, message, a generated error ID and stack trace. Success and error paths must produce the same entry shape, long URLs should be truncated, and the logs should be ready to ship to a central log aggregation backend.

generic_title: Expose host CPU, memory and disk usage metrics from the service
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service, I want to monitor the whole machine it runs on, not just the JVM: current system-wide CPU usage, total and free physical memory, and free/total disk space per volume. It must work cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows) without me maintaining OS-specific code or shelling out to external programs, and any library used must be compatible with a closed-source commercial product. Expose these as metrics that a monitoring system can scrape and alert on (e.g. disk below 10% free).
title: Expose host CPU, memory and disk metrics for the printer farm server
prompt: In this 3D-printer farm management app, the dashboard server often runs on a small box next to the printers. I want to monitor that host: system-wide CPU usage, total and free physical memory, and free/total disk space (print files are staged locally before upload). It must be cross-platform without OS-specific code of my own, use only commercially-compatible licensed libraries, expose the values as scrapeable metrics, and raise a warning in the dashboard when free disk drops below a configurable threshold.

generic_title: Propagate request context into background thread pool logs
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot app we put session IDs and usernames into the logging context for web requests, but much of the work runs on thread pools, timers and custom executors, where that context is either missing or stale (inherited from an earlier task). I want a reliable way to carry the context, or better a trace/correlation ID, from the submitting thread into every background task and clear it afterwards, without each developer having to remember manual copy calls. Add a test proving that a background task logs the right request ID even when the pool thread was reused.
title: Carry correlation IDs from user actions into printer background tasks
prompt: In this 3D-printer farm management app, user actions (e.g. starting a print, uploading a file) kick off work on scheduler threads and message-handling threads that talk to the printers. Logs from that background work have no idea which user or request triggered it. I want every user action to get a correlation ID that is propagated automatically into scheduled jobs, executor tasks and printer message handlers, appears on every log line and trace span, and is cleared afterwards so reused threads never show a stale ID. Add a test covering a reused worker thread.

generic_title: Monitor JVM memory usage without forcing garbage collection
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot application we currently log memory usage by calling System.gc() and then reading Runtime total/free memory, which we've been told is a bad idea. I want proper JVM monitoring instead: heap and non-heap usage per memory pool, garbage collection counts and pause times, and memory used after GC, exported as metrics a monitoring system can graph and alert on. We especially want to see the spike when a large XML export is generated from the database, and alert if post-GC heap stays above a threshold.
title: Monitor JVM memory and GC during heavy report queries
prompt: In this BI / SQL reporting dashboards app, large report queries and exports cause memory spikes, and today we only notice when the server falls over. I want proper JVM monitoring without calling System.gc(): heap and non-heap usage per pool, GC counts and pause times, and heap used after collection, exported as metrics a monitoring system can graph. Tag a metric with which report query was running when memory crossed a configurable threshold, and alert if post-GC heap stays high for several minutes.

generic_title: Centralize request logging and timing instead of per-controller code
generic_prompt: In this Spring MVC app, every controller method copies the same block: log request start, URL, each parameter name/value, then the JSON response and how long it took. I want that removed from controllers and handled generically: one component that logs URL, method, parameters, response status, response size and duration in milliseconds for every request, plus records request duration as a latency metric per endpoint so we can see slow routes. Sensitive parameters like passwords must be masked.
title: Add centralized request logging and per-endpoint latency metrics
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want consistent request logging and timing for both the REST and GraphQL APIs without adding code to each controller or data fetcher. One component should log path (or GraphQL operation name), method, parameters, response status and duration, with passwords and JWTs masked, and record per-endpoint/operation latency histograms so we can see whether article feeds or comment listing are slow. Add tests that a login request is logged with the password masked.

generic_title: Count views with an invisible tracking pixel
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot web app, I want to implement a "web bug": a 1x1 transparent image that can be embedded in pages (and HTML content shown elsewhere) so each load records a view. Every hit should record timestamp, referrer, user agent and an anonymized client identifier, be resistant to browser caching (cache-busting parameter and no-cache headers), and the image must return instantly even if recording is slow. I need to be able to count views per item and per day, so send the events to a proper analytics/event store rather than grepping access logs.
title: Count article views with an embeddable tracking pixel
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want to know how often each article is actually read, including when an article is embedded or syndicated elsewhere. Add an endpoint serving a 1x1 transparent image keyed by article slug; each load records a view event with timestamp, referrer, user agent and an anonymized visitor identifier, defeats caching, and responds immediately even if recording is slow. Then expose view counts per article per day to the article's author, backed by a proper analytics/event store rather than access-log parsing.

generic_title: Persist application log entries to a database without changing call sites
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot app, every class logs through the standard logging facade with a static logger. I want all log entries (timestamp, level, logger, thread, message, exception, and any context like user ID) also written to a database table so support staff can search them, without changing any existing logging calls. Writes must be batched/asynchronous so logging never slows down requests, failures of the log store must not break the app, and old entries should be purged after a retention period.
title: Store application log entries in a searchable database table
prompt: In this e-commerce shop app, support staff want to search what happened to an order across the catalog, cart, ordering, delivery and billing modules. Without touching existing logging calls, route all log entries (timestamp, level, module/logger, thread, message, exception, and context such as order ID) to a database table in addition to the console. Writes must be asynchronous and batched, an outage of the log store must not break checkout, entries older than a retention period are purged, and a simple admin page lists entries filtered by order ID and level.

generic_title: Track web server thread pool usage over time
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service, I suspect the embedded web server's request thread pool is leaking threads over time. I want to record the number of busy and total request-handling threads, the max configured, and the connection queue length, sampled continuously and exported as metrics so I can graph them and alert when busy threads approach the max. No manual console access should be needed, and the solution should also tell me whether the reverse proxy's connection limit in front of us is lower than our thread max.
title: Track request thread pool saturation for the redirect service
prompt: In this URL shortener app, redirects sometimes stall under load and I suspect the embedded web server's request thread pool is being exhausted or leaking. I want metrics for busy and total request threads, the configured maximum and pending connections, exported continuously so they can be graphed and alerted on when busy threads approach the max, and an endpoint or dashboard showing current saturation, all without connecting a manual JVM console.

generic_title: Mask credit card numbers in all log output
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot web app we must be PCI compliant, but an upstream system sometimes returns full card numbers and those responses are logged at debug level in many places. I need card numbers (13 to 19 digits, with or without spaces/dashes) masked transparently in every log line, including exception messages and structured fields, without replacing every logger in the codebase. Keep the first 4 or last 4 digits visible, and add tests proving that no full card number can reach any log output.
title: Mask payment card numbers in every log line
prompt: In this e-commerce shop app, the billing module is internal today but we are preparing for card payments and must not leak card numbers into logs. I need card numbers (13 to 19 digits, with or without spaces or dashes) masked transparently in every log line from every module, including exception messages and structured context fields, without changing existing logger calls. Keep only the last 4 digits visible and add tests that log billing and ordering events containing card numbers and assert none appear unmasked.

generic_title: Let admins change log levels at runtime from the UI
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot application, an administrator should be able to change the log level (e.g. INFO, DEBUG, WARN) of the whole app or of specific packages from an admin screen, and the change should apply immediately without a restart. Expose a secured API to list current levels and set/reset them, optionally with an expiry so DEBUG automatically reverts after 30 minutes, and if several instances are running, the change should apply to all of them. Record who changed what in an audit log.
title: Let admins change log levels at runtime via a secured API
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) Quarkus API, I want administrators to raise or lower log levels at runtime, globally or for specific areas such as article or user handling, without redeploying. Add secured endpoints (admin role via the existing JWT auth) to list current levels and set/reset them, with an optional expiry after which DEBUG reverts automatically, propagate changes to all running instances, and record who changed what and when.

generic_title: Export database connection pool metrics
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot application the database connection pool is auto-configured, so I never build it myself. I want the pool's metrics (active, idle and pending connections, max size, connection acquisition time, usage time and timeouts) exported to our metrics registry so a monitoring system can graph them and alert when connections run out, ideally without abandoning auto-configuration and redefining the whole datasource by hand.
title: Export database connection pool metrics from the Conduit API
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) Quarkus API backed by a relational database, I want visibility into the connection pool: active, idle and waiting connections, max size, acquisition time and acquisition timeouts. Export these as metrics a monitoring system can scrape and alert on when the pool is exhausted, keep the existing framework-managed datasource configuration, and add a health check that reports degraded when waiting requests exceed a threshold.

generic_title: Add logout and session timeout handling to a login-protected web app
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot web app users can already log in with a form, but there is no way to log out. I need a logout action that invalidates the server-side session and any remember-me cookie, redirects to the login page with a message, and prevents the back button from showing protected pages. Sessions should expire after a configurable idle timeout, an expired session should redirect to login with a "session expired" notice, and admins should be able to force-logout a specific user.
title: Add staff login, logout and session timeout to the clinic
prompt: In this veterinary clinic management app, all pages for owners, pets, vets and visits are currently open to anyone. Add staff login with logout that invalidates the session and redirects to the login page with a message, protect the owner, pet and visit forms, and expire idle sessions after a configurable timeout with a "session expired" notice. An admin should be able to force-logout a staff member, and the back button must not reveal protected pages after logout.

generic_title: Compute an aggregated application health status from internal metrics
generic_prompt: In this Spring application I want a status endpoint that returns FATAL, WARN or HEALTHY based on internal metrics and health data: heap used vs committed, peak thread count, free disk space against a threshold, plus our custom counters. Read these values in-process (not by calling our own HTTP endpoints), recompute the status periodically, make the thresholds configurable, and include the contributing values and which rule triggered in the response so operators can see why.
title: Add an aggregated health status endpoint for the Conduit backend
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) app, operators want a single status endpoint returning HEALTHY, WARN or FATAL. Compute it in-process from JVM metrics (heap usage, thread count), free disk space for the local database file, database connectivity and app counters such as failed logins per minute. Recompute periodically, make thresholds configurable, and return the contributing values and the rule that triggered so it is clear why the app is degraded.

generic_title: Emit structured JSON logs with embedded JSON payloads
generic_prompt: In this Java REST application, I want logs written as one JSON object per line for a log aggregation pipeline. When I log a JSON payload (e.g. an incoming message), it should be embedded as a nested JSON object in the log event, not as an escaped string, so downstream tools can query its fields directly. Other events should include timestamp, level, logger, thread, message, exception and context fields. Keep the existing logging calls working, and add a test that parses a log line and reads a nested field.
title: Switch the Conduit API to structured JSON logs
prompt: In this blog / social (RealWorld Conduit) Quarkus API, I want logs emitted as one JSON object per line so they can be shipped to a log aggregation backend. Each line should include timestamp, level, logger, thread, message, exception and context such as user and article slug, and when we log a request or event payload it must be embedded as a nested JSON object, not an escaped string. Keep plain-text logs for local development, and add a test that parses a log line and reads a nested field.

generic_title: Detect and report slow SQL queries
generic_prompt: In this Spring application using an ORM over a relational database, I want to find queries that take too long. Log any statement exceeding a configurable threshold (e.g. 200 ms) with its SQL, bound parameters (with sensitive values masked), duration, row count and the calling code location, and record query duration as metrics per query type so I can graph the slowest ones and alert on regressions. It should have negligible overhead when queries are fast.
title: Detect and report slow SQL queries across shop modules
prompt: In this e-commerce shop app, which uses plain JDBC across catalog, cart, ordering, delivery and warehouse modules, I want to find slow queries. Log any statement over a configurable threshold with its SQL, masked parameters, duration, row count and the module that issued it, and record per-module query duration metrics so the slowest areas can be graphed and alerted on. Overhead must be negligible for fast queries, and add a test that a deliberately slow query is reported.

generic_title: Route HTTP access logs through the application logging pipeline
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service, HTTP access logs currently only go to a plain file written by the embedded web server. I want every request's access log line (method, path, status, response time, client IP, user agent) to flow through the same logging framework as the rest of the app so it gets the same appenders, rotation and shipping. Avoid hand-rolling a servlet filter if the server's access log hook can be bridged; add a dedicated logger name for access logs, a sensible pattern, and a test that a request produces exactly one access log event.
title: Send Conduit API access logs through the app's logging framework
prompt: In this RealWorld blog API (REST and GraphQL), access logs are only written to a flat file by the embedded web server, if at all. I want every request to the articles, profiles, comments and GraphQL endpoints to emit one access log event (method, path, status, duration, client IP, user agent, authenticated username when present) through the application's logging framework under a dedicated logger name, so it shares appenders and rotation with the rest of the logs. Prefer bridging the server's access log hook over a custom filter, and add a test that a request yields exactly one access event.

generic_title: Report whether ORM second-level cache served each query
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service using an ORM with a second-level and query cache, I can only guess whether a query hit the cache by checking if SQL appeared in the log. I want proper visibility: expose cache hit, miss and put counts per entity region and for the query cache as application metrics, log at debug level when a lookup is served from cache, and add an endpoint or metrics output I can check after a request. Include a test that loads the same entity twice and asserts one miss followed by one hit.

generic_title: Expose database connection pool usage for monitoring
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot app, I need my monitoring system to see how the database connection pool is doing. Expose the pool's active, idle, total and pending-thread counts plus max size and connection acquisition time as metrics, and add a lightweight status endpoint that returns them as JSON for an external checker to poll and alert on (e.g. warn when over 80% of connections are in use). Add a test that the endpoint reflects a borrowed connection.
title: Expose connection pool usage for each reporting datasource
prompt: In this BI dashboard server, reports run SQL against user-configured datasources through pooled JDBC connections. I want operators to see pool health per datasource: active, idle and total connections, threads waiting for a connection, max pool size and connection acquisition time. Expose these as application metrics tagged by datasource name, and add an admin-only endpoint returning them as JSON so an external monitoring system can poll it and alert when a pool is over 80% utilized. Add a test that borrowing a connection is reflected in the numbers.

generic_title: Include request body in error logs for REST endpoints
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot REST API, our global exception handler logs the exception, URL and user, but debugging would be much easier if the JSON request body were logged too. Capture the request payload (with a size cap) so it can be included when an exception is logged, mask sensitive fields such as passwords and tokens, and correlate the entry with a request ID. The body must still be readable by controllers. Add a test that a failing POST produces an error log containing the masked payload.

generic_title: Keep application log files safe for external log rotation
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot service deployed on Linux, ops wants the system's log rotation tool to manage all log files instead of the logging library's built-in rotation. Configure the file logging so it cooperates with external rotation: either reopen the log file when it is moved (on a signal or periodic check) or use copy-truncate safely, ensure no lines are lost or written to the rotated file, and disable built-in rotation. Provide the sample rotation config and a test that writing continues to the new file after a rename.

generic_title: Write log output to a separate file per user
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot web app, support needs each user's activity in its own log file, e.g. logs/<username>/app.log, so they can hand a single user's log to an investigation. Route log events to per-user files based on the authenticated user of the current request (set once per request, cleared afterwards), keep normal app-wide logging unchanged, roll the per-user files daily, and close idle appenders so file handles don't leak. Add a test that two users' requests end up in separate files.

Collect these from the platform management beans, publish them as metrics to a time-series backend, and also allow a periodic snapshot to be written to a log. The interval should be configurable and add a test for the collector.

generic_title: Build an endpoint to page through very large log files
generic_prompt: In this Spring Boot admin service, we have a built-in log viewer that loads the entire log file into memory and falls over on multi-gigabyte files. Replace it with an API that pages through a log file without reading it all: build (and cache) an index of line offsets, support fetching a range of lines by number, tailing the last N lines, and a simple substring search that streams results. Keep memory use bounded regardless of file size, and add tests with a generated large file.

generic_title: Report progress for large file uploads

title: Generate link previews for article URLs in the background

title: Deduplicate article reindex jobs

title: Direct-to-storage uploads for article cover images

title: Scoped upload access for writers on mobile

generic_title: Save canvas drawings as images in object storage

title: Upload cropped avatar images sent as data URIs

title: Profile avatar uploads with size and type validation

title: Thumbnails for images embedded in articles

generic_title: Validate uploaded images by their magic bytes

title: Verify avatar uploads are real images by content
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) API, let users upload a profile avatar instead of only pasting an image URL. generic_title: Switchable storage backend: local disk vs object storage

title: Pluggable storage for article images

generic_title: Store uploaded photos in object storage and keep their URLs

title: Article cover images in object storage
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) API, let authors attach a cover image to an article. generic_title: Protect the server from oversized uploads
generic_prompt: In this Express API, users upload profile images and other pictures. Client-side validation exists, but an attacker can bypass it and send huge files to fill up the server's disk. title: Enforce upload limits for profile images
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) API, add a profile image upload endpoint for the logged-in user, and make it safe against abuse: enforce a hard maximum file size that aborts the upload as soon as it is exceeded (without buffering the full body), allow only image content types, allow only one file per request, keep a per-user storage quota, and clean up any partial file if the request is aborted. title: Import a blog cover image from a URL

title: File attachments on articles

title: Proxy-offloaded image uploads with content-hash paths

title: Live comment stream for articles

title: Push notifications for new motivational content

Add a read-through cache in front of single-article lookups: on a miss, load the article from the database and populate the cache; when an article is updated, deleted, favorited or unfavorited, invalidate its cached entry so the next read is always current. The cache should be a shared service usable by multiple API instances, configurable via environment variables, and covered by tests showing an edit is visible immediately.

generic_title: Add per-user, per-endpoint rate limiting shared across processes
generic_prompt: In this Express API running as a cluster of processes, add a rate-limiting middleware I can attach per route, e.g. login allows 5 requests per 20 seconds. Limits must be enforced across all processes and instances, so the counters need a shared store rather than process memory. I also need per-user overrides: for the same endpoint, one user may get 5 requests per 20 seconds and another 10. Identify callers by authenticated user id when available, otherwise by client IP. Return 429 with a Retry-After header when the limit is exceeded.
title: Rate-limit document creation across server processes
prompt: In this pastebin service there are no user accounts, so anyone can create documents. Add a rate-limiting layer for the document creation and fetch endpoints, keyed by client IP, with different limits per route (e.g. 5 creates per 20 seconds, more generous limits for reads) and the option to raise limits for specific allow-listed clients. The service may run as several processes or instances, so counters must live in a shared store, not process memory. Return 429 with a Retry-After header when exceeded.

generic_title: Notify a separate Python worker when a webhook arrives
generic_prompt: This Express API receives POST webhooks at an endpoint. Whenever a job comes in, a separate Python service running on another host needs to be notified so it can process it. Today I publish locally and it only works on my machine. Set up proper cross-service messaging: the API publishes a message with the request params and body to a named channel or topic on a shared message broker, the Python consumer subscribes from its own server, and messages should not be lost if the consumer is briefly offline. Document the message format and configuration.
title: Notify a fulfillment service when a purchase is made
prompt: In this e-commerce store backend, a separate fulfillment service written in Python runs on another host and needs to know whenever a customer completes a purchase. Add cross-service messaging: after a purchase is recorded, publish a message with the purchase id, user id, line items and totals to a topic on a shared message broker that the Python service subscribes to. Messages must survive the consumer being briefly offline. Document the message schema and add configuration via environment variables.

Implement a server-side cache for these upstream responses: serve from cache while max-age is fresh, revalidate with If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since once stale and reuse the cached body on 304, and store entries in a shared cache so multiple instances benefit. Add tests for fresh, stale-revalidated and changed responses.

generic_title: Retry calls to an external feed API with backoff after rate limits

title: Sync articles to an external feed service with retries

title: Generate PDF transaction statements in the background

Add an upload endpoint that stores the file in object storage and returns a pending attachment id, then let the create and update article endpoints accept attachment ids and link them to the article. Only the uploader may attach their own pending files, article responses list attachment URLs, and a scheduled cleanup removes pending uploads never attached within 24 hours.

generic_title: Store base64-encoded receipt images sent in JSON as files
generic_prompt: In this Express API, clients create expense records by posting JSON that includes a receipt image as a base64 data URL. Storing that string in the database is wasteful. Before saving, decode the data URL, validate the declared MIME type and size, store the file in a storage backend under a generated name, and replace the field with the stored file reference before persisting the record. Expose an endpoint to download the receipt, and reject malformed data URLs with a 400.
title: Accept receipt images on transactions as base64 data URLs
prompt: In this peer-to-peer payments (Venmo-style demo) app, I want users to optionally attach a receipt image when creating a payment or request transaction. The frontend sends it inside the JSON body as a base64 data URL. Decode it, validate MIME type and size, store the file in a storage backend under a generated name, and save only the file reference on the transaction. Add an endpoint so the sender and receiver can view the receipt, and return a 400 for malformed data URLs.

generic_title: Stream multi-file uploads directly to object storage
generic_prompt: In this Express API, users upload several files in one multipart request, and I want each file streamed straight to object storage without buffering whole files in memory or writing them to disk. While streaming, inspect the first chunk to verify the file type and compute a checksum. Support multiple files per request with per-file and total size limits, abort and delete already-uploaded parts if any file fails validation, and respond with the stored key, size and checksum of every file.
title: Stream multiple blog images directly to object storage
prompt: In this blogging platform (blogs, writers, editors) app, writers should be able to upload several images for a blog draft in one multipart request. Stream each file straight to object storage without buffering in memory or on disk, check the file type from the first bytes, and compute a checksum while streaming. Enforce per-file and per-request size limits, roll back already-stored files if any one fails, attach the stored images to the writer's blog, and return the key, size and checksum for each.

generic_title: Import records from an uploaded CSV file without keeping the file
generic_prompt: In this Express API, users should be able to upload a CSV file and have a record created for each row, without the file itself being stored. Accept the upload in memory or as a stream, parse it with headers, validate each row, and insert valid rows in a transaction. Respond with a summary: rows imported, and for invalid rows the line number and reason. Enforce a size limit, reject non-CSV files, and handle large files by streaming rather than loading everything at once.
title: Bulk-create payment requests from an uploaded CSV
prompt: In this peer-to-peer payments (Venmo-style demo) app, I want a user to upload a CSV of payment requests (columns: receiver username, amount, description) to request money from many contacts at once. Parse the uploaded file as a stream without saving it, validate each row (user exists, amount positive), create the request transactions for valid rows, and respond with counts plus line number and reason for each rejected row. Enforce a file size limit and reject non-CSV uploads.

generic_title: Store original images plus generated thumbnails on upload
generic_prompt: In this Express API, when a user uploads an image I need two things stored: the original image and a resized thumbnail (e.g. max 300px wide). Accept the upload, generate the thumbnail with an image processing library, store both in the storage backend, and keep a record linking original and thumbnail with dimensions and content type. Provide endpoints to fetch either version, validate file type and size, and delete both when the image is deleted.
title: Generate thumbnails for article images on upload
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) app, authors should be able to upload a header image for an article. Store the original and generate a resized thumbnail (max 300px wide) for article lists, keeping both in a storage backend with a record linking them to the article along with dimensions and content type. Return both URLs in article responses, validate type and size, and delete both files when the image is replaced or the article is deleted.

generic_title: Import a file from a shared link into cloud storage
generic_prompt: In this Express API, users paste a link to a document hosted elsewhere (e.g. a shared file link from a file-sharing service) and the API should copy that file into our own cloud storage. Add an endpoint that takes the URL, resolves share links to a direct download, streams the content into a storage bucket without saving it locally, records name, size and content type, and returns the stored file id. Enforce a maximum size, a timeout, and only allow http(s) URLs to non-private addresses.
title: Create pastes by importing a remote file link
prompt: In this pastebin app, I want users to create a paste from a link to a text file hosted elsewhere (a raw file link or a shared file link) instead of copy-pasting. Add an endpoint that takes the URL, follows redirects, streams the content (text types only) into the document store under a new key, and returns the paste key. Enforce a maximum size and timeout, only allow http(s) to public addresses, and return clear errors for unreachable links or unsupported content.

generic_title: Add file deletion to database-backed file storage
generic_prompt: In this Express API, uploaded files are stored as chunks inside the database through a storage engine, and upload plus retrieval by filename already work. Add a DELETE endpoint that removes a file by id, deleting both its metadata and all its chunks, returns 404 if it does not exist, and only allows the uploader to delete. Also delete files automatically when the record that references them is removed, so no orphaned chunks remain.
title: Allow deleting article attachments from file storage
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want authors to attach files to articles and to delete them again. Add a storage backend for uploaded files, an endpoint to upload an attachment to an article, and a DELETE endpoint that removes an attachment by id (metadata and stored content), returning 404 if missing and 403 if the caller is not the article's author. When an article is deleted, remove all its attachments so no orphaned files remain.

generic_title: Answer HTTP requests from an event-driven backend
generic_prompt: In this Express API, I'm moving to an event-driven design: the HTTP layer publishes commands to a message broker and several worker services consume them. The problem is the user's HTTP request still needs a response. Implement request-reply over the broker: the API publishes a command with a correlation id and reply destination, waits (with a timeout) for the matching result event and returns it, and falls back to 202 Accepted with a status URL when processing takes too long. Include a sample worker that consumes the command and publishes the result.
title: Process purchases through a message broker with request-reply
prompt: In this e-commerce store backend app, I want purchase creation handled by a separate worker instead of inside the HTTP handler. When a user checks out, publish a 'create purchase' command to a message broker with a correlation id and reply destination; a worker consumes it, validates stock and prices, writes the purchase and publishes a result event. The API waits for the matching reply up to a timeout and returns it, otherwise returns 202 with a status endpoint. Include the worker and keep the existing purchase endpoints' contracts.

generic_title: Forward messages from a queue consumer to connected browsers
generic_prompt: In this Express API, a background consumer reads messages from a message queue topic, and every consumed message should be pushed in real time to the browsers that care about it. Set up a realtime layer attached to the HTTP server, structure the code so the consumer module can emit to clients without importing the server directly (a shared realtime service), and route each message only to clients subscribed to the matching channel. Handle consumer restarts and clients that reconnect.
title: Push comment events from a queue to article readers in real time
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want new comments to appear live for readers of an article. When a comment is created, publish an event to a message queue; a consumer module reads those events and pushes them over a realtime connection to clients currently viewing that article. Structure it so the consumer emits through a shared realtime service rather than reaching into the server setup, deliver only to subscribers of that article's channel, and handle reconnects.

generic_title: Send push notifications from the API through a push provider
generic_prompt: In this Express API, an admin dashboard needs to send push notifications to users' browsers and devices through a push notification service. Add a notification module that calls the provider's REST API with the server key from configuration, supports sending to all subscribers, to a segment, or to specific user ids, and an admin endpoint to compose and send a notification (title, message, link). Store a log of sent notifications with the provider's response id and surface provider errors cleanly.
title: Send push notifications to users from an admin endpoint
prompt: In this motivational content app backend (WhereIsMyMotivation) app, I want admins to send push notifications (e.g. a new mentor or topic was added) to users' devices through a push notification service. Add a notification module that calls the provider with credentials from configuration, supporting all users, users who follow a given topic, or specific user ids, plus an admin-only endpoint to compose title, message and deep link. Store a log of sent notifications with the provider's message id and return clear errors on failure.

generic_title: Authenticate websocket connections with the existing JWT
generic_prompt: In this Express API, REST routes are protected with JWT bearer tokens, and I'm adding a websocket gateway for realtime features. Clients must send the same access token when connecting (in the handshake auth payload, not the URL). Verify it on connection, reject invalid or expired tokens, attach the user to the socket, and protect individual message handlers. Handle token expiry on long-lived connections by disconnecting with a clear reason so the client can refresh and reconnect.
title: Add authenticated live notifications for followed authors
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want users to get live notifications when an author they follow publishes an article or someone comments on their article. Add a websocket channel that authenticates with the same JWT used by the REST API (sent in the handshake payload), rejects invalid or expired tokens, and joins each user to their own channel. Emit notifications from the article and comment creation code paths, and disconnect with a clear reason when the token expires.

generic_title: Add realtime rooms that clients can create and join
generic_prompt: In this Express API, I'm adding a websocket gateway and need rooms: a client can create a room, join or leave it, and messages sent to a room reach only its members. Track membership on the server, broadcast join/leave events with the member list, validate that a client is in a room before it can send to it, and clean up empty rooms. Include an endpoint to list active rooms with member counts.
title: Add live discussion rooms per article
prompt: In this blogging platform (RealWorld Conduit) app, I want readers of an article to chat live while viewing it. Add a websocket gateway where each article slug is a room: clients join when opening an article and leave when closing it, messages go only to that room, and join/leave events broadcast the current viewer count. Only authenticated users may send messages; anyone can join to read. Clean up empty rooms and expose an endpoint returning the live viewer count for an article.

generic_title: Send web push notifications that open a specific page when clicked
generic_prompt: In this Express API, I send browser push notifications through a push messaging service, and they arrive fine, but clicking them does nothing. Each notification should open a specific page of the site (e.g. the item it is about). Update the server-side send code to include the click-through link in the notification payload in the format the web client expects, add a service worker click handler that focuses an open tab or opens the link, and allow only same-origin links.
title: Notify followers with clickable web push when an article is published

Add an endpoint to register a user's web push subscription, send notifications through a push messaging service when an article is created, include the article link in the payload so the click opens it, and remove subscriptions the provider reports as expired.

generic_title: Validate push registration tokens before storing them
generic_prompt: In this Express API, clients send their push notification registration token to the server to be saved for later sends. Anyone could post a random fake token. Add a token registration endpoint for authenticated users that validates the token with the push service (e.g. a dry-run send) before storing it, associates it with the user and device, deduplicates, and removes tokens the service later reports as invalid or unregistered when real sends fail.
title: Register customer device tokens for order push notifications

Add an endpoint for logged-in users to register a device push token, validating it with the push service (a dry-run send) before saving so fake tokens are rejected, storing it per user and device without duplicates. Send a notification when a purchase is created, and delete tokens the push service reports as invalid or unregistered.

generic_title: Record visitor browser, language and country
generic_prompt: In this Express API, I need to know who is visiting: browser name and version, OS, device type, preferred language and country. Add middleware that parses the user agent, reads the accept-language header, resolves the country from the client IP (respecting proxy headers), and records anonymized visit events. Provide an endpoint with aggregated breakdowns by browser, language and country over a date range. Don't store raw IP addresses.
title: Track paste views by browser, language and country

When a document is viewed, record a visit event with browser and OS from the user agent, preferred language, and country resolved from the client IP (trusting proxy headers), without storing raw IPs. Add an endpoint returning view counts per paste key and aggregated breakdowns by browser, language and country for a date range.

generic_title: Emit realtime events from REST controllers and services
generic_prompt: In this Express API, I have REST endpoints and want to push events to connected clients over websockets when things change (e.g. a record is created or updated). Create a realtime service that owns the websocket server and can be injected or imported into controllers and services, so any route can emit events to all clients, to one user, or to a channel. Avoid circular dependencies and keep REST handlers working in tests without a socket server.
title: Notify writers live when editors publish or reject their blogs
prompt: In this blogging platform (blogs, writers, editors) app, writers should be told immediately when an editor publishes or sends back their blog, and editors should see new submissions arrive. Add a realtime service owning the websocket server that controllers can call, authenticate connections with the existing access tokens, emit to the specific writer on publish/reject and to all editors on submission, and keep the REST handlers testable without a socket server.

generic_title: Transcribe microphone audio from the browser in near real time
generic_prompt: In this Express API, the browser records microphone audio and sends it to the server, and I want text back. Accept audio chunks over a websocket (or a recorded blob via upload), forward them to a speech-to-text service with streaming recognition, and send interim and final transcripts back to the client as they arrive. Handle audio format/sample rate conversion, a maximum session length, and errors from the speech service.
title: Let users submit voice notes that are transcribed to text

generic_title: Send an SMS when a new record is added

title: Text users when they receive a payment request

generic_title: Fall back to SMS when a push notification is not delivered
generic_prompt: In this Express API, users are notified by push when they have a registered token, otherwise by SMS. The problem is the push service reports success even when the browser is closed and the message just sits in a queue. Implement delivery confirmation: the client acknowledges receipt to an endpoint, and if no acknowledgment arrives within a configurable window (e.g. 60 seconds), send the same notification via SMS. Track each notification's status and avoid sending both when the ack arrives late.
title: Notify customers about purchases by push with SMS fallback

Send a push notification if they have a registered device, have the client acknowledge receipt to an endpoint, and if no acknowledgment arrives within a configurable window, send the message by SMS instead. Users without a device get SMS directly. Track each notification's channel and status, and avoid double sending when an acknowledgment arrives late.

title: Push a notification to all subscribers when a blog is published

I want an agent that finds the payer policy criteria that apply: ingest the payer policy PDFs we store, chunk them by section, embed them into a vector index with metadata (payer, plan, effective dates, CPT ranges), and on request retrieve and summarize the applicable criteria as a checklist with section citations. Filtering by payer, plan and effective date must happen before semantic ranking so we never cite an expired policy. Answers must say when no policy matches rather than guess. No patient data may be sent to the LLM for this step. Add tests for the metadata filtering and a management command to re-index when a policy is updated.

title: Evidence agent mapping chart documents to authorization criteria

Given an authorization request with its criteria checklist, I want an evidence agent that reads the attached clinical documents (visit notes, imaging reports, medication history), extracts supporting facts and maps each fact to a criterion with the page and quote it came from. Output should be structured JSON validated against a schema, with each criterion marked met / not found / conflicting. PHI handling matters: redact identifiers not needed for the criteria before sending text to an LLM, keep everything in our region, and never store model outputs outside the request record. Show results in a side-by-side view where coordinators can accept or reject each mapping. Include tests with synthetic chart documents.

title: Add a conversational shopping agent that fills the cart via tool calls
prompt: In this Spring Boot DDD e-commerce shop, the catalog, cart, order and delivery logic live in separate domain modules. I want a conversational shopping agent endpoint the storefront can call from a chat panel: the customer describes what they want and the agent uses tool calls against our own domain services (find products in the catalog, get product details, add item to cart, change quantity, remove item, show cart) to build the cart. It must never place the order or touch payment; it stops at a cart summary and the customer finishes through the normal order flow. Keep conversation state per cart, cap tool calls at 8 per turn, validate every tool argument against the domain model, and return clear errors for unknown products. Respect the module boundaries; the agent belongs in its own module that talks to the others through their public APIs. Add tests with a scripted LLM stub covering 'add two of the cheapest coffee' and a product that doesn't exist.

Steps and tool outputs should be persisted as an investigation log the analyst can read, the agent should stop after 12 tool calls, and the result is a draft the analyst confirms or rejects. Once a homeowner accepts a heat pump quote, we want to collect a deposit (typically 10-20%) on the spot, either by card or by sending a payment link, and later invoice the balance net of incentives. The tool is often offline in basements, so payment requests must queue and sync when connectivity returns, and no raw card data may touch our app. Each payment must be tied to the quote version accepted so a later quote edit doesn't change what was paid. Add a payments module behind an interface, a sync worker, and tests for offline queuing, duplicate submission and partial refunds when incentives change the total.

title: Build an ESG disclosure agent that maps evidence to frameworks

Build an LLM agent in FastAPI whose tools search the client's uploaded evidence (utility bills, HR policies, supplier lists, travel data), compute emissions using our factor tables, look up requirements in our framework library, and write draft disclosures section by section with each figure linked to evidence. Guardrails: never estimate a figure without labelling it an estimate and citing the method. Evaluate on 15 past client reports, measuring figure accuracy and coverage of required disclosures.

Build the agent that each day reads the business's CRM export and booking system, identifies who to contact (unanswered quotes, customers due for service, happy customers to ask for reviews), drafts personalized messages and proposes a daily plan. Tools: list_contacts, get_visit_history, get_open_quotes, draft_message, schedule_send. The owner approves the plan in a dashboard (bulk approve, edit, skip); nothing is sent without approval during the first 30 days, after which owners may auto-approve message types. Guardrails: respect opt-outs and quiet hours, never offer discounts above the owner's limit, stop on any reply and hand off to the owner. Evaluate on historical data: would the agent's picks have matched the customers who actually rebooked?

generic_title: Two-way SMS for local business outreach

Add two-way texting: provision a number per business, send scheduled messages, receive replies into a shared inbox in our app, detect STOP and other opt-out keywords, honor quiet hours in the customer's time zone, and track delivery status. Business owners must register for carrier compliance before sending. Rate-limit per number and add tests for opt-out handling.

generic_title: Build the personal insurance shopping agent
generic_prompt: We are replacing a human insurance shopper with an agent. A household uploads current auto/home/renters policies and answers a short questionnaire; the agent compares their coverage to their situation, requests quotes from carrier rating endpoints we integrate with, and produces a recommendation explaining coverage gaps, deductibles and price differences in plain language. Tools: get_policy_summary, get_household_profile, request_quote(carrier, coverage), compare_quotes. A licensed agent must review and approve any recommendation before it is shown, and only humans bind policies.
